COVID: The rise of Esport in Lockdown

By: Sinethemba Nogude | Production

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
As the world of sports is in a idefinite hiatus , we look at how Esport is challenging the status quo , with its meteoric rise in popularity during this time.

Unique Selling Point:
By now you are missing the thrill of your favorite football team scoring a last gasp winning goal, the rush of seeing a mercurial winger making a final dash for the try line ,or even the unmistakable roar of an F1 engine.But in the past few months Athletes and sports fanatics have been left high and dry with most sporting codes taking an indefinite hiatus( locally the PSL,All domestic rugby , as well all domestic cricket), and the projections don’t look good, global sporting revenue is set to take Losses in the tens of billions of dollars.Athletes and sports organizations alike are having to adapt to these new realities, with salary cuts and slashed earnings from broadcasting deals organizations and athletes are taking things online.Local Brian Habana has launched a digital platform called Match Kit , whereby any athlete can tap into this platform to connect and market themselves to sponsors, connect with fans , sell merchandise and raise funds for their charity foundations.

Summary:
But In the midst of this pandemic,only one “sporting “code has emerged, The popularity of Esport has been on a rapid rise in past few years,but during the global shut its popularity has sky rocketed ,gaming revenue is projected to reach 159 billion dollars just this year, that’s 3 times the revenue the entire music industry is projected to make, and South Africa is not being left behind,the industry is seeing a surge in Esport uptake by ordinary South Africans( partly thanks to internet providers coming to the party and increasing internet speadd),this is no longer the realm of the “geeks” ,South African are especially taken by Esport simulation games ,we are seeing ordinary South Africans Climb up international gaming boards, and turning heads.
Streaming platform like Twitch are making it easy for South Africans to connect to the world,to put it into perspective: A recent Esport game (FIFA ) where Trevor Noah played Cassper Nyovest drew in a South African record online audience, which is unprecedented in South Africa .
Esport is an industry that everyone is buying into, Netflix is now broadcasting actual eSport on its platform and it is proving to be a success, DSTV broadcast GINX TV AFrica , a dedicated 24 hour Esport channel, many experts are even pointing to an almost inconceivable notion -That Esport will in a few decades Challenge global tournaments like the FIFA World Cup as the most popular spectator sports.


Further information:
Treatment :

The treatment for the story will be edgy, high paced and will have a “grunge “ feel to it .We will focus on making links interesting and will involve a lot of visual inputs : gaming orientated transitions, actual game graphics and will explain and contexualise certain gaming aspects in an interesting but understandable manner. Whilst the story will Have story will have a lot of visual input ,this will be done in a way that will not alienate the traditional Carte Blanche viewer, but will hopefully educate older viewers on this subculture.

Script:


Esports
-Short gaming montage-
V/O You could be forgiven for thinking that you’ve wandered into an alternate universe since the outbreak of COVID-19 Where fans are still packing arenas cheering their sporting heroes on ,But this is not an actual a Formula one race and these are not actual F1 drivers and this is not a real circuit …it is all virtual… this is ESport.
V/O Whilst the Covid 19 pandemic threw the sporting world a curve ball, with major sporting codes like football , Rugby and motorsport STARTING TO RETURN BUT only BEHIND CLOSED DOORS ,traditional sports is not only facing a new reality of empty stadia but also the ACCORDING esports analytical firm Esports Charts dwindling viewership numbers during the global shutdown.
v/O Electronic sports or Esports describes the world of competitive, organized video gaming where individuals and teams armed with consoles and PC’s take part in round robin games simulating sporting codes like football and motorsport ,but also tactical shooter games ,strategy games and fighter games.
Link As the world of sports struggles , and Esports taking off , it makes sense for these industries collide ,but instead you are seeing a convergence of the two
V/O Once considered the realm of the geek, Esport is rapidly shaking off this tag, as sporting mega stars like Charles le Clerc ,Raheem Sterling and Ben stokes take part in highly competitive Esport tournaments ….And people can't get enough ;The recent Formula one Erace series which pitted F1 drivers against each racing across virtual circuits drew a viewership of 20 million viewers across both online and on television in just its first 3 races, whilst the English Premier league invitational league tournament which saw top footballers competing in online soccer tournaments was viewed by over 150 million people world wide.

V/O South African GT racer Dave Perel was one of the first professional athletes in the world to make the cross over to Esport ,initially competing in virtual racing to maintain a competitive edge during the off season.Little did he know how fast Esport would take off during the global shut down.
Upsound Dave Perel :I stumbled upon a game called Gran Turismo which I have been a fan of my whole life and I started to use Gran turismo to learn how to be a race driver or improve as a racing Raheem Sydriver …[mac chips in] no matter what I was racing I just came back to the play station, I would work on my consistency, trying to improve racing lines and I started understand the connection between racing in the real world , because I would use a steering wheel and I realised there was a direct connection , ofcourse its virtual and you’re playing a game there is no doubt about it, but the inputs you apply, especially these days are almost the same as in real life.
Upsound David Perel : When Covid happened the sim racing world exploded because all these real racing drivers who initially didn’t have time for the simulator were flocking to the simulator to spend their free time on and race online and race against fellow competitors. We’ve had sort of blossoming in the last two months
Upsound: And its not kids who are contacting us , its people in their 20s and 50s.
Upsound Dave Perel d its been surreal for me, I have coached and recently I have helped out formula one driver Jenson Button and Chales Le Clerc … I was on the phone with my brother and it pops up on my screen Charles le clerc is calling me and I said I have to go Charle Le Clerc is calling me.. how is that not insane
V/ O what he thought was a passtime soon grew into a business.
Upsound Dave Perel: I’ve always had this idea to blend sim racing and and racing … And I started these Coach dave meme which turned into a side business,//I was coaching sim racers on how to be better sim racers and I was using my experience.
V/ O This is a billion dollar industry with millions of adoring fans world wide ...in 2019 popular Esport game League of Legends held a tournament which drew viewership of over 100 million , Surpassing popular traditional sports like basketball, tennis, and Baseball.
V/O And at the centre of it all is a whole new breed of sporting star- the Esport Athlete , 24 year old Julia robson has been competing for over ten years and is one of the top names in the local Esport scene.
Upsound: For my birthdays , instead of getting clothes and make up I would get a PC case or an external harddrive.
V/O After pursuing her studies at the University of the Western Cape , Julia made a radical decision to turn professional
Upsound Julia 0:28 I was studying dentistry for two years before I inevitably when I dropped out to pursue my career in Esports
V/O Julia She packed up her bags and moved to Johannesburg to get closer to the Esport scene.
Upsound Julia Robson :02:00luckily my mom is quite supportive …I think my mother understood that it is something I have been pursuing for a long time and have passion for.
V/O Speciallising in first -person shooter games ,a type of Esport whose gameplay involves shooting virtual enemies and other targets as the player views the action through the eyes of the character they are controlling and just like any other athlete Julia spends hours practising online competing -testing herself against the best in the world.
Upsound Julia Robson :lot of gamers spend time online competing , but considering how much time and efforts gamers put in getting to the top of their game , for example , I competed in counter strike global offensive and I have 5000 hours on my account so far and that’s only in one game I compete in.
V/O whilst competing in tournaments online can be lucrative ,Most of Julia’s income is generated through her social media presence,using various online streaming platforms.
V/O On a daily basis she has to create Esport content for her growing online subscription base.
Upsound : As a twitch streamer , I stream my gaming content, and video content, I go live every few days a week and I just create a nice interactive experience where I play a game and interact with my audience, some people support the twitch streamer with a subscription and I get a potion of that and the other is viewers that donate , that is another avenue and then advertisement and brand deals.Thats a very large potion of it for me.I prefer to monetise my content through what I create from brand deals and marketing
V/O By creating gaming themed video diaries or vlogs, she has travelled the world.
Link Macfarlane :As Esports cements itself in popular culture , global investors , brands ,media outlets and consumers are starting to pay attention.
Upsound Costa : viewership is dropping in certain sports and therefore the value for money they are putting in sports they are not really receiving from an eye ball point of view,but Esport viewership is rising and constantly , some stats show that in certain demographics Esports is watched more than regular sports … it makes sense for those viewers to move into esports is a good investment for them.
V/O Konstantinos Tzingakis CEO of Red oxygen , a mobile game development studio in Johannesburg is not surprised by the rapid rise of Esports during the Covid-19 Pandemic
Costa 03:06 So many of the giants Globally have started showing Esport for a while , and entire studios like Ginx and others have , supersport has been showing it for some time , with a lack of sport they have been able to focus a lot on that, if nothing else , it has created a lot of awareness in people, Esport is a thing and moving forward as the world starts to move forward , Esports will now be on the radar for most people.
04:00 Esport as a career is viable and its become more and more viable each year,tournaments award players up to 20 million dollars, the prize money is fantastic even in South Africa the top ranking player in SEsco has earned a million rands , as Esports is viewed ...Those size pools are going to increase.
V/O As Esport globally punches above its weight , Esport executive Nathaniel Slabbert reckons that the future of spectator sports lies within Esport.
Upsound :Nathaniel 03:59 Yes, I firmly believe from a personal point of view , is an will overtake sports eventually, I you just look at society in general… a lot of these kids could end up playing video games and they are not even going out and kicking the ball about which is a problem ,
V/O But as countries begin to examine paths towards loosening stay-at-home restrictions and sports events being played behind closed doors , will the industry be able to sustain its newfound gains...that remains to be seen
David Perel 25:45 Upsound :I think live sports in general are going to get a reckoning in the next few months and we are going to see which ones are going to survive this level of disruption.


- End-

metadata.Unique Selling Point: By now you are missing the thrill of your favorite football team scoring a last gasp winning goal, the rush of seeing a mercurial winger making a final dash for the try line ,or even the unmistakable roar of an F1 engine.But in the past few months Athletes and sports fanatics have been left high and dry with most sporting codes taking an indefinite hiatus( locally the PSL,All domestic rugby , as well all domestic cricket), and the projections don’t look good, global sporting revenue is set to take Losses in the tens of billions of dollars.Athletes and sports organizations alike are having to adapt to these new realities, with salary cuts and slashed earnings from broadcasting deals organizations and athletes are taking things online.Local Brian Habana has launched a digital platform called Match Kit , whereby any athlete can tap into this platform to connect and market themselves to sponsors, connect with fans , sell merchandise and raise funds for their charity foundations.
metadata.Summary: But In the midst of this pandemic,only one “sporting “code has emerged, The popularity of Esport has been on a rapid rise in past few years,but during the global shut its popularity has sky rocketed ,gaming revenue is projected to reach 159 billion dollars just this year, that’s 3 times the revenue the entire music industry is projected to make, and South Africa is not being left behind,the industry is seeing a surge in Esport uptake by ordinary South Africans( partly thanks to internet providers coming to the party and increasing internet speadd),this is no longer the realm of the “geeks” ,South African are especially taken by Esport simulation games ,we are seeing ordinary South Africans Climb up international gaming boards, and turning heads. Streaming platform like Twitch are making it easy for South Africans to connect to the world,to put it into perspective: A recent Esport game (FIFA ) where Trevor Noah played Cassper Nyovest drew in a South African record online audience, which is unprecedented in South Africa . Esport is an industry that everyone is buying into, Netflix is now broadcasting actual eSport on its platform and it is proving to be a success, DSTV broadcast GINX TV AFrica , a dedicated 24 hour Esport channel, many experts are even pointing to an almost inconceivable notion -That Esport will in a few decades Challenge global tournaments like the FIFA World Cup as the most popular spectator sports.

Whilst the story will Have story will have a lot of visual input ,this will be done in a way that will not alienate the traditional Carte Blanche viewer, but will hopefully educate older viewers on this subculture.
